title: feat(app-shell): switch the sharing_rule client validator on at the edit door
body:
Fixes #7612

Clause-②: no

`AUTHOR_SHAPE_ONLY_TYPES` gated the client validator OFF on the `sharing_rule`
**edit** door. This switches it on. The switch is the small half: the order's first
instruction was a falsification, because objectui#6982 measured that this boundary was
**not** removable even after the ADR-0010 envelope keys landed upstream, and triage's
R+318 audit found the card's own description of the mechanism no longer matched the
code while being unable to say whether the decoration still arrived.

## 1. The falsification, before any edit

**Question:** what does the edit path hand the validator today, on `c2f0f4832`?

**The card's quoted mechanism is gone.** It quoted the draft assembly as
`layered.effective` spread under `client.getDraft().item`, stripping nothing. The
inline `getDraft()` spelling: 0 hits in `ResourceEditPage`. Same-subject control in
the same command: the `client.getDraft` call it was describing is still there, at
three sites. So the zero is a real absence, not a dry corpus.

**Triage's four strip spellings were looking for the wrong name.** `stripDiagnostic`
/ `stripServerOnly` / `omitDiagnostic` / `delete ... _diagnostics`: 0 hits across
`packages/app-shell/src`. Same-subject control in the same command: the bare word
`_diagnostics` matches 27 files in that same corpus. The strip exists under a name
none of the four covers — `stripReadDecorations`, reached through `extractDraftBody`.

**What the assembly actually is.** Each of the three edit-mode merge sites builds
`{ ...baseline, ...draftReal }` where `baseline` is the layered `effective` layer and
`draftReal` is `extractDraftBody(draftResp)`. The two remaining `setDraft` paths (reset
and discard-draft) read the layered layers only. So there are exactly two ingress
halves, and both are closed:

| half | carries a decoration? | why |
|:--|:--|:--|
| layered `effective` baseline | no | the framework's layered read computes `_diagnostics` onto the ENVELOPE, as a sibling of `effective`, and serves its three layers raw — it never calls the per-item decorator. The objectui client forwards `effective` verbatim and lifts `_diagnostics` off the envelope. |
| pending-draft body | stripped | `extractDraftBody` removes the spec's own exported `METADATA_READ_DECORATIONS` before the body is merged. Landed by objectui#7603, hoisted to one function by objectui#8181. |

**Live schema reading** against the resolved `@objectstack/spec` (a probe run, not a
recollection): the decoration list is `_diagnostics` and `_draft`; every ADR-0010
envelope key is declared and typed (two of them refuse a wrong VALUE, which is a
declaration, not an unknown key); both decorations are refused with
`unrecognized_keys` at the **root**, which is the path length the `serverSchema.required`
root-cure cannot reach; the same served body with the decorations taken off is accepted;
and a genuinely undeclared key riding along is still refused. So the schema is exactly
as strict as it was — the thing that changed is upstream of it.

⇒ **The decoration does not reach the validator.** The release condition is met, and
the switch is safe. Had it still arrived, the order was to stop and report; it does not.

## 2. What changed

- `AUTHOR_SHAPE_ONLY_TYPES` is now **empty**. The mechanism stays, and its header now
  states the bar a type must meet to be listed, and which of the two key families each
  cure belongs to — declare the envelope, or remove the decoration before the gate.
  It points at the instruments instead of restating their answers, which is what this
  block got wrong before: it described an edit path that had stopped existing.
- The `ResourceEditPage` comment that described `AUTHOR_SHAPE_ONLY_TYPES` as having
  members is corrected in the same commit — this change is what made it false. Added
  by the `domain:ui#2` execution seat at the implementing dev's own request: the file
  was otherwise explained only in passing, by the lint ablation in section 4.
- ⛔ **No schema was loosened and no decoration list was reconstructed locally.** That
  would be the second de-facto contract the spec's own header warns about.

## 3. The pin, converted rather than replaced

The waiting case in `clientValidation.optOuts.test.ts` asserted that the edit door let a
`_diagnostics`-carrying body through. That was true only because no gate ran. Keeping it
on an open door would have required the schema to TOLERATE the decoration, so it is
converted to assert the opposite and honest fact: **both doors refuse a raw decorated
body, and both accept the stripped one the edit path actually assembles.** Its
counter-measurement keeps it from being satisfied by a schema that refuses everything.

The card also asked for the live read-path probe to be re-run against a
decoration-stripped draft. The page test named for the read-decoration strip is
parameterised by metadata type and now covers `sharing_rule` end to end: it drives the
real editor with a decorated pending draft and reads what the **real** gate was handed.
A clean draft is accepted with no banner; an `accessLevel` outside the declared enum is
refused on the edit door. That second case is the control — it proves the gate ran, so
the first case's silence is a measured verdict rather than a validator that never fired.

## 4. Evidence — RED before, GREEN after

Every reading below was taken **after** the last commit to what it measures; the tree was
verified equal to `7181f6f2e` with nothing unstaged before the final sweep.

**RED, with the switch still `['sharing_rule']` on disk (verified in the same command):**

- read-decoration page probe — `exit 1`, both new cases fail with
  `the gate never judged the merged pending draft`. The two pre-existing `page` cases
  stayed green, so the parameterisation did not break them.
- converted opt-out pins — `exit 1`, `2 failed | 19 passed`.

**GREEN, after the switch:** both files together, `exit 0`, `25 passed`.

**Gates, re-run as the last action before the push, tree clean at `7181f6f2e`:**

| gate | exit |
|:--|:--|
| `check:control-bytes` | 0 |
| `check:new-line-citations` | 0 |
| `check:changeset-presence` | 0 |
| `check:changeset-no-major` | 0 |
| `check:changeset-claims` | 0 |
| `check:pending-changeset-literals` | 0 |
| `check:test-path-roots` | 0 |
| `check:vi-mock-specifiers` | 0 |
| `check:vi-mock-inherit` | 0 |
| `check:vi-mock-override-shape` | 0 |
| `check-governed-queue-guard --test` | 0 — `NOT GOVERNED`, 5 paths checked |

**Build, types and tests** (through the shared verify lock, whose own `VERDICT
command-exit` line is the reading in both cases):

- dependency closure `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build` then
  `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` — `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The
  package's `type-check` compiles the test tsconfig too, so the edited tests are typed.
- full package `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/` from the repo root —
  `VERDICT command-exit 0`, `736 passed`, `7304 passed | 1 skipped`.

**Lint, narrowed and the narrowing measured rather than asserted.** Targeted eslint over
the four changed files reports 64 problems, 3 of them errors. Those errors are **not
mine**: with only `ResourceEditPage.tsx` reverted to its base content on disk — the
mutation proven by object hash and by an anchor grep going to 0, the restore proven by
object hash plus an empty `git diff HEAD` and `git diff --cached` — base reports the
identical 64 problems and the identical 3 errors, at line numbers 2 lower, which is
exactly the two lines this branch adds above them. The three pieces the narrowing needs:
the population is the file set eslint selects from its own config, which its `--format
json` output counts at 5177 files; the targeted run covers the 4 files this branch
touches; and the invariance is that this repo enables no type-aware linting — no
`parserOptions.project`, no `projectService`, with the control that the config does
define rules — so nothing in this diff can move the verdict of a file it did not touch.

## 5. Acceptance notes

- **The A / B / C decision on the card is still the maintainer's, and this PR is option
  B.** The card states plainly that whether to gate this door at all is author-facing
  behaviour on a security-metadata surface. Option B is what the objectui#6982
  implementer recommended, what the card's author recommended, and what the dispatching
  seat ordered once the falsification passed — but none of those three is the maintainer.
  The PR stays draft. If the answer is A, the revert is one line plus the pins.
- Nothing here is exploitable either way: the server validates this type regardless. What
  the edit door buys is that the refusal reaches the author in the editor instead of on
  Save.
- `AUTHOR_SHAPE_ONLY_TYPES` now has no members. Whether an empty mechanism should be
  retired outright is a separate judgement about this file, deliberately not taken here:
  it would delete a documented boundary that a future strict schema may need, and the
  mode argument it reads is load-bearing for `view` regardless. Noted, not filed.
- Same package as objectui#9954 (`hooks/`, `layout/`, `console/` — disjoint directories,
  untouched here). Whichever lands second is type-checked against the other's code and
  owes the re-verification on the merged ref.
